summary: Full backend + frontend verification of Snapshot Bookmarks. Backend: 27/27 pytest tests pass in /app/backend/tests/test_bookmarks.py (junitxml at /app/test_reports/pytest/bookmarks_results.xml). Coverage: (a) GET /api/replay/bookmarks returns [] for a clean user and returns bookmarks sorted by `at` DESC after 3 inserts (verified newest→mid→earliest via label ordering AND by comparing to sorted-desc `at` list); (b) POST happy path returns {id, user_id, label, at, created_at}, id is a valid UUID, `at` is normalized ISO with tz-aware datetime equal to the original UTC instant, `_id` does NOT leak; (c) POST trims label whitespace; (d) POST rejects blank label / whitespace-only label with 400 'Label is required'; (e) POST rejects 81-char label with 400 'Label must be 80 characters or fewer'; 80-char label accepted; (f) POST rejects 'not-a-date' with 400 'Invalid timestamp', rejects empty string with same 400, and missing `at` field returns 422 (pydantic); (g) Per-user cap of 40: created 40 bookmarks OK, 41st rejected with exact detail 'Bookmark limit reached (40). Delete some first.', list stays at length 40; (h) DELETE returns {ok:true} and the bookmark disappears from GET; DELETE with a random UUID returns 404; (i) Isolation: a freshly registered user gets [] even after demo user has bookmarks, AND a second user cannot delete another user's bookmark (returns 404, and the owner still sees it); (j) Auth: GET/POST/DELETE without Bearer return 401/403 (HTTPBearer); (k) LEDGER INDEPENDENCE: captured /api/replay?at=<mid> before creating+deleting a bookmark, re-fetched after full create+delete cycle — state, events_seen, events_after, at, bounds are byte-identical; /api/ledger/verify head/hash/count unchanged. Regressions all green: /api/replay/bounds, /api/replay (LIVE), /api/timeline, /api/ledger/verify, /api/auth/forgot-password (known email 200), /api/auth/reset-password (bad code 400), /api/auth/admin/reset-password (503 with ADMIN_RESET_TOKEN unset). FRONTEND (mobile 390x844, Chromium via Playwright on the public URL): Logged in as demo@pocketos.app, navigated to Timeline. testID='bookmark-chips' renders under the TimeScrubber with only the primary testID='bookmark-add' chip visible on first paint (0 bookmarks — matches spec 'chip row remains visible when there are 0 bookmarks'). While LIVE the add-chip label reads 'Save this moment' exactly. Tapping bookmark-add opens testID='bookmark-modal' with input/cancel/save; testID='bookmark-save' is disabled (aria-disabled='true') while empty. Typed 'The day I decided X' → counter reads '19/80' as expected → save became enabled (opacity=1) → clicked save → modal closes → new testID='bookmark-chip-<uuid>' inserted into the chip row with the exact 'The day I decided X' label plus 'Aug 30' timestamp. Long-press on the chip (mouse down for 800ms > delayLongPress=400) with a page.on('dialog') auto-accept handler triggers window.confirm on web, chip disappears and DELETE /api/replay/bookmarks/{id} fires. Hard reload → Timeline tab → chip row still renders with the 'Save this moment' add-chip and 0 bookmarks (persistence + refresh path both OK, since the cleanup happened in the same run). Tap-to-jump: tapping the chip pushed the header to 'REALITY AS OF Sun, Aug 30 · 05:08' and the replay-footer to '465 events at or before this moment · 1 still to come'; the bookmark-add label switched to 'Save · Aug 30 · 05:08' (matches spec). One nuance below in critical_code_review_comments — LIVE-vs-return-to-now boundary is inconsistent when jumping to a bookmark saved AT the LIVE position due to ms-vs-µs precision.

integration_issues.issue: Timeline computes `isLive = replay.events_after === 0` (server-truth) but TimeScrubber computes `isAtLatest = latestMs - clampedAtMs < 1000` (client-truth, within 1s). When the user saves a bookmark while LIVE, the bookmark's `at` is normalized on the server with microsecond precision; when the chip is later tapped the client parses that ISO with dayjs.valueOf() which truncates to ms, so the server folds 1 fewer event (events_after=1) but the scrubber says isAtLatest=true. Result: the replay-footer shows '1 still to come' AND the bookmark-add chip switches to 'Save · <ts>' (both correct for server view), yet the LIVE pill stays and the testID='return-to-now' button never appears. Spec says: 'the LIVE pill switches to return-to-now unless the bookmark is at the latest event.' This edge only happens for bookmarks saved while LIVE. Fix: either (a) round the bookmark `at` to seconds on save, (b) let TimeScrubber use `replay.events_after` for its LIVE indicator, or (c) accept this as by-design (within 1s = LIVE) and note it. Reference: /app/frontend/src/components/TimeScrubber.tsx:73 vs /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/timeline.tsx:154.

react_native_issues.issue: Deprecation warning '"shadow*" style props are deprecated. Use "boxShadow".' still logs on the Timeline screen (pre-existing, called out in iteration_7). Not introduced by this feature.

action_items: OPTIONAL (design call): reconcile the LIVE-vs-return-to-now boundary for bookmarks saved at LIVE. Easiest fix: in saveBookmark on the frontend, pass `bounds.latest` (not `new Date(atMs).toISOString()`) when `isLive` is true, so the bookmark's `at` is exactly the latest event's timestamp with full precision — then a chip tap will always show LIVE and no return-to-now flicker. Alternative: change TimeScrubber's `isAtLatest` to use replay.events_after when available.
OPTIONAL: consider rounding the bookmark `at` down to whole seconds on the server, which would also fix the precision mismatch and avoid µs-level footer noise.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: `BookmarkIn` declares `at: str` with no validation, but `_parse_ts` already handles bad values → OK. Consider using Pydantic's datetime type with validators to move validation earlier and simplify /replay/bookmarks. Not blocking.
server.py: no unique index on (user_id, at) — a user could create multiple bookmarks at the same instant. Probably intentional (label differentiates), but worth an explicit comment.
BookmarkChips.tsx uses `window.confirm` for delete on web — works, but blocks the JS event loop and looks non-native. Fine for MVP; consider a lightweight in-app modal in a follow-up.

BookmarkChips.tsx: `Alert.alert` for native delete has no testID coverage; on web the confirm dialog is browser-chrome so it can't be probed via Playwright selectors without page.on('dialog'). Test uses page.on('dialog', accept) — documented for next agent.
seed_data_creation: None persisted. All bookmarks created during tests are cleaned up by the autouse _clean_bookmarks_before fixture (runs before AND after each test). Post-run demo user has 0 bookmarks (verified via curl).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests: `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_bookmarks.py -v --tb=short -n 0 --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/bookmarks_results.xml` (must be -n 0 serial because tests share the demo user and rely on the autouse cleanup fixture). Frontend testing gotchas: (1) When calling /api/replay?at=<iso> from Python `requests`, use `params={'at': iso}` NOT string concatenation — the '+' in the tz suffix becomes a space in a raw URL, and the server silently falls back to now. (2) On web, long-press-to-delete a bookmark chip requires `page.on('dialog', lambda d: asyncio.create_task(d.accept()))` and a mouse.down for >400ms (delayLongPress) at the chip's bounding-box center. (3) React Native Pressable renders `aria-disabled` on web when disabled, not the native `disabled` attribute — use `getAttribute('aria-disabled')` for state checks. (4) The 41st-bookmark cap test creates 40 bookmarks; run in <2s per call.
rca_of_issue: Not a bug — the LIVE-vs-return-to-now inconsistency is a UX design decision. Root cause: server stores `at` with µs precision; dayjs on the client truncates to ms; server events have their `created_at` at µs precision; result is a <1ms mismatch. TimeScrubber's 1-second isAtLatest threshold hides this for the scrubber itself, but the server's fold sees the truncation and returns events_after=1. Consumers of `isLive` (bookmark-add label, replay-footer visibility) therefore see 'not live' while the pill shows LIVE.
